set.body:
Objective:
Revise the planned ntab architecture so it consumes the ScalaFIM-incubated Frame relational foundation instead of implementing a second metadata column store, expression language, query planner, grouping system, ordering layer, or scalar interpreter.

Ownership after the rebase:
Frame owns runtime scalar schemas, named-tuple typed promotion, scalar column storage, expressions, relational logical plans, filtering, grouping keys, joins, ordering, local reference execution, logical normalization, and generic source/sink capabilities.
ntab owns neuroimaging FeatureId and FeatureRef values, feature catalogs, exact volume/surface/parcel support, resource resolution plans, feature codecs, support-aware numerical flatten/rebuild, grouped feature reducers, contributor lineage, drill-down, and domain adapters such as group-ntab.

Dependency and naming law:
ntab depends on Frame artifacts using their current ScalaFIM names plus the necessary ScalaFIM image, surface, and atlas modules. Frame may use the ScalaFIM package prefix while incubating, but it never imports or depends on ScalaFIM domain modules. If Frame is extracted and renamed later, ntab changes dependency coordinates/imports mechanically; relational semantics and the ntab ownership boundary do not change. dataset, group, mvpa, multivar, and lower domain modules do not depend back on ntab; leaf bridges sit above both sides.

Design constraints:
- Large NeuroVol, SurfaceField, and parcel payloads are not arbitrary Arrow cells. Frame rows carry stable typed feature references or compact descriptors; ntab resolves payloads explicitly.
- Exact support remains a scientific invariant. No implicit resampling, topology correspondence, or parcel alignment enters generic Frame operations.
- Dynamic discovery remains the primary workflow. Typed Frame schemas and bound feature handles are proofs obtained at runtime boundaries.
- Code generation remains optional and non-foundational.

Acceptance:
- docs/plans/ntab.md, module relations, and proposed build edges reflect the current ScalaFIM Frame dependency and the later controlled-rename path without duplicated relational concepts.
- Every former ntab core type is classified as delete, replace with Frame, keep in ntab, or move to a leaf adapter.
- An end-to-end API sketch shows DynamicFrame inspection, typed Frame metadata filtering/grouping, and then ntab feature resolution/reduction/lineage.
- The plan names the precise Frame foundation capabilities required before ntab implementation can start.
- No implementation is started against speculative Frame APIs.
